requirements.text: An account owner can create an active provider pixel in their account.
Supported providers are Meta Pixel and Google Analytics with validated IDs.
Pixels attach to LinkPilot-rendered link pages and CTA overlays.
Public React emits fixed provider-specific script shapes only after consent; arbitrary snippets and Google Tag Manager are rejected.
Pixels can attach to bio pages, link pages, and CTA overlays and fire only for documented, consented surface events.
Pixel attachments use allowlisted page-view, button-click, or lead-submit triggers on owned LinkPilot surfaces only.
Meta renders each validated pixel ID once and uses account-specific trackSingle PageView calls.

acceptanceCriteria.text: No provider request or script runs before granted visitor consent.
A trigger fires only for its attached owned resource and configured event.
Arbitrary script, markup, Tag Manager, and remote injection fields do not exist.

observedBehaviors: The tracking-pixel screen presents a resource table and create action.
Provider and status columns are visible.

implementationEvidence.description: Fixed-provider validation, consent-gated tracking, and public-page projection deduplication pass behavior coverage.
implementationEvidence.reference: tests/Feature/LinkPages/LinkPageTest.php (including duplicate Meta ID projection); tests/Feature/Overlays/OverlayDeliveryTest.php; tests/Feature/Analytics/AnalyticsTrackingTest.php; php artisan test (168 tests, 10,347 assertions)

implementationEvidence.description: A consented public page with a repeated Meta identifier and one distinct Meta identifier queued one init and one account-specific trackSingle PageView per distinct ID; no global track call was emitted.
A zero-pixel quota account retained the create dialog and rendered its form-level plan limit.

TrackingPixelTriggersTest and AnalyticsTrackingTest passed in focused coverage; the full isolated Laravel suite passed 428 tests and 15,151 assertions, with one ClamAV-dependent PDF-delivery case skipped.

Before tracking consent, Meta/GA4 scripts and requests were absent. After consent, page-view and click events dispatched, while lead-submit fired only after accepted response; vendor requests were intercepted before delivery and disposable test pixels/rules/leads were removed.
